bios.name: Andrew Devine
bios.metaDescription: Andrew Devine is a partner at Blanchet LLP who handles product liability, environmental, class and mass action, commercial, construction, investment, and CERCLA-related disputes.
introduction: Andrew Devine is a litigator who handles hard-to-resolve disputes with a strategic, tech-savvy, and practical approach.

Andrew represents multinational corporations, manufacturers, construction owners and general contractors, banks, and investment companies in product liability, environmental, class and mass action, personal injury, commercial, construction, and investment matters in federal and state courts and arbitrations across the country.

He starts with the result a client is after, shapes an efficient and focused path to get there, and executes. Clients rely on him to manage complexity, including motion and appellate briefing, removal and jurisdictional issues, large-scale document review, depositions, and expert practice.

Andrew brings particular depth to environmental disputes, including the defense of claims involving groundwater and the remediation of sites under CERCLA. He is also comfortable with the technology that defines modern litigation, using experience and e-discovery tools to surface the facts that matter.
representativeExperience: Represented a construction project owner in state and federal lawsuits seeking damages and injunctive relief relating to breach of construction agreement and alleged tort claims. Won a preliminary injunction hearing, obtained dismissal and summary judgment dismissing tort and certain contract claims, secured affirmance on appeal, and resolved the remaining claims on favorable terms.

Represented a chemical company in a class action alleging that contamination from a remediated CERCLA site caused personal injuries to nearby residents under common law tort theories. Following removal to federal court, obtained complete dismissal and secured affirmance on appeal.

Represented a group of potentially responsible parties that cooperated in the cleanup of a CERCLA site in a New York State court action brought by a neighboring landowner alleging that remedial operations damaged adjacent property. Obtained dismissal and secured affirmance on appeal.

Represented a general contractor in a construction, breach of contract, and lien dispute with a surety and subcontractor. Obtained near-complete recovery through a favorable settlement reached before discovery began.
Represented a financial services company in an investment suitability lawsuit filed by a customer of a former investment advisor. Obtained complete dismissal.
Represented a financial services company in an investment suitability arbitration before the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority. Resolved the matter on favorable terms.
Represented an insurer in ERISA disputes with an insured in federal court lawsuits. Obtained complete dismissal.
Represented a petroleum wholesaler in payment disputes across the East Coast, achieving substantial recoveries from counterparties.

bios.name: Craig Nolan
bios.metaDescription: Craig Nolan is a partner at Blanchet LLP focused on trials, appeals, government investigations, enforcement matters, white collar defense, complex civil litigation, regulatory matters, and product liability litigation.
introduction: Craig Nolan is a trial attorney, appellate advocate, and former federal prosecutor who represents clients at trial and in government investigations and enforcement matters, white collar defense, commercial disputes, product liability litigation, regulatory matters, and appeals.

With more than 30 jury trials and dozens of appeals before federal appellate and state supreme courts, Craig has served as White Collar Crimes Chief at the U.S. Attorney's Office for Hawaii, State's Attorney for Vermont's third-largest county, and a civil litigator at leading firms in Vermont and North Carolina.

Craig brings the perspective of a federal prosecutor, trial attorney, and appellate advocate to matters that require early control, nuanced judgment, and demonstrable trial-readiness. He is especially valuable where litigation risk, government scrutiny, and appellate issues overlap, and where trial counsel is needed to assist or replace litigation counsel.

bios.name: Joel Blanchet
bios.metaDescription: Joel Blanchet is a trial lawyer representing sophisticated clients in commercial, environmental, product liability, and other high-stakes disputes.
introduction: Joel Blanchet is a trial lawyer and problem solver who represents companies, legal departments, executives, and other sophisticated clients in high-stakes disputes across the country. His work spans commercial litigation, environmental and toxic-tort matters, product liability, securities, intellectual property, bankruptcy, and government-facing disputes.

Before launching Blanchet LLP, Joel spent more than a decade as a partner in the litigation department at Kirkland & Ellis and later helped lead the litigation practice at Phillips Lytle. He has handled trials, arbitrations, appeals, and complex pretrial proceedings across industries and jurisdictions.

Joel stays close to the work and to the client. He brings practical business judgment to serious disputes, develops the record with trial in mind, and focuses the strategy on the result the client actually needs.

bios.name: Wayne Myers
bios.metaDescription: Wayne Myers is a founding partner of Blanchet LLP and a former senior federal prosecutor focused on high-stakes litigation, complex civil disputes, government and grand jury investigations, white collar matters, cybercrime, and internal investigations.
introduction: Wayne Myers is a founding partner of Blanchet LLP. A trial-ready litigator and former senior federal prosecutor, Wayne represents companies, executives, professionals, and individuals in high-stakes litigation, complex civil disputes, government and grand jury investigations, white-collar matters, and internal investigations. He also handles select criminal matters.

Wayne held some of the highest positions in the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Hawaii, including First Assistant U.S. Attorney, First Deputy U.S. Attorney, Criminal Chief, and Appellate Chief. His remit covered the full range of federal litigation: criminal prosecutions, civil litigation, appeals, sensitive investigations, and office operations. He worked regularly with Department leadership in Washington, federal agencies, law enforcement, the judiciary, and community stakeholders.

Before Hawaii, Wayne served as an Assistant U.S. Attorney in the Northern District of New York, where he was Chief of the Albany Branch Office, supervised Criminal Division AUSAs, managed a 40-person office, and built a nationally recognized cybercrime program.

Over the course of his career, Wayne has tried more than a dozen cases to verdict, supervised dozens more, personally handled hundreds of federal court hearings, and appeared in hundreds of grand jury proceedings. He knows the federal system from the inside: how prosecutors evaluate cases, how agents build investigations, how grand juries operate, where investigations and cases hit stress points, when Main Justice gets involved, and how federal judges assess contested facts and law.

Wayne’s experience spans national security and terrorism, financial crime, procurement fraud, health care fraud, public corruption, cybercrime, environmental crime, crimes against children, violent crime, firearms and explosives offenses, narcotics, and cryptocurrency. He has handled high-level national security and counterterrorism matters and held high-level federal security clearances.

Unusual among litigators, Wayne is genuinely fluent in the technology itself. He is comfortable in the details of digital forensics, networks, electronic evidence, cryptocurrency, and cyber investigations, not just the law that surrounds them. He has particular depth in digital evidence and surveillance, including the Stored Communications Act, ECPA, CFAA, search warrants, Fourth Amendment issues, and cross-border evidence collection.

Before joining the Department of Justice, Wayne practiced at Kirkland & Ellis LLP in Chicago and New York, where he handled complex commercial litigation, bankruptcy litigation, trade-secret matters, and high-stakes business disputes.

Wayne’s philosophy as a lawyer is simple: keep what matters, lose what does not, and know that telling the difference is the work. He is decisive under pressure and quick on his feet, as ready to make the call in a crisis as to make the argument in court.
